entries.title: Psalms 39:1
segments:
Keep my mouth; be silent. 
 
  While the wicked is before me; under the pressure of present suffering, the psalmist was greatly tempted to impatient complaints respecting God's dealings with him.  See

.  To guard against these, he resolved to impose upon himself entire silence in the presence of the wicked. 
 
Those who continue to wait upon God by humble prayer and supplication, and in the diligent use of all the appointed means of grace, will find in the end that the Lord hears and answers, and does exceeding abundantly for them according to all their wants.

entries.title: Psalms 39:2
segments:
Even from good; from the fear of saying something wrong, he refrained from uttering any thing, even that which was right, and might have been profitable. 
 
Great circumspection in conversation, especially in the presence of the wicked, is a duty; but neither fear nor favor should hinder us from speaking that which is good, or making known our wants and offering our requests in prayer and supplication to God.

entries.title: Psalms 39:3
segments:
While I was musing; in silence.  The suppression of his feelings within his own bosom only made him more vehement, till he could no longer refrain, but spoke to God as in the following verses. 
 
The blessings which God bestows upon his people in answer to prayer, encourage many to pray and to put their trust in him.

entries.title: Psalms 39:6
segments:
They; who seek this world as their chief good. 
 
Those who seek the world as their chief good, find that it leaves them when they most need support; while it may be the ruin of those who come after them.

entries.title: Psalms 39:9
segments: Thou didst it; his afflictions were sent by God.

entries.title: Psalms 39:11
segments: Like a moth; as a moth destroys a garment, so health and beauty are consumed by the afflicting hand of God.

entries.title: Psalms 39:12
segments:
A stranger--a sojourner; one on a pilgrimage; passing quickly through this to the eternal world. 
 
As the continuance of man upon the earth is like a vapor which appeareth for a little time and then vanisheth away, his treasure should be laid up in heaven and his affections should be there; then, when absent from the body he will be present with the Lord, and the God whom he has served will be his inheritance and his portion for ever.
